citations.statement: Uniform empirical-vs-population squared-difference comparison over a bounded function class controlled by its sup-norm covering number.
citations.verbatim_statement: For any policy π and state-action pairs {(s_i,a_i)} generated i.i.d. from ρ × π, and ε_c < 1, with probability at least 1−δ, for any g_1 and g_2 we have E_{ρ×π}[(g_1(s,a)−g_2(s,a))²] ≤ (2/n)∑_{i=1}^n(g_1(s_i,a_i)−g_2(s_i,a_i))² + (32/(3n))log(2N_F(ε_c)/δ) + 10ε_c, where N_F(ε_c) is the ε_c-covering number of F.

citations.statement: Measurable maximum theorem: measurability of the value function and existence of a measurable maximizing selector for a Caratheodory objective over a weakly measurable compact-valued correspondence.
citations.verbatim_statement: Let X be a separable metrizable space and (S,Σ) a measurable space. Let φ:S⇒X be a weakly measurable correspondence with nonempty compact values, and suppose f:S×X→R is a Carathéodory function. Define m(s)=max_{x∈φ(s)}f(s,x) and μ(s)={x∈φ(s):f(s,x)=m(s)}. Then m is measurable; μ has nonempty compact values; and μ is measurable and admits a measurable selector.

The core's symbol L_n(E) declares its codomain as {pi in Delta(A)^X : supp pi(.|x) subseteq supp pi_ref(.|x) for every x}, and def:common-experiment states a learner 'is supported on pi_ref at every context'. So L_n(E) IS the reference-SUPPORTED finite-objective class: encode it with the PolicySupportedOn conjunct. This is law-independent (the condition depends only on the PUBLIC pi_ref), and it is WITHOUT LOSS, not a narrowing: def:minimax-risk supplies the public contextwise support repair S_ref, which is Borel measurable BECAUSE the supports carry the standing discrete/Borel structures of design decision f2.5-discrete-support, maps every measurable full-simplex learner into L_n(E), and never increases regret (off-support regret is +infinity under the extended convention, repaired regret is finite). Supported learners are themselves full-simplex learners, so the two infima are EQUAL and the common value is a nonnegative real. The plan therefore encodes the supported class as the definition and the full-simplex equality as a proved companion, exactly as the core states. J_underscore_n is likewise DIAGNOSTIC ONLY and its domain is exactly the reference-supported policies (core: 'no real-valued off-support evaluation is intended'); it does not define pi-hat. def:prediction-polytope-learner.notes: Construction: prediction polytope F, empirical loss L_n, sequential-lexicographic ERM f-hat, empirical seminorm ||.||_n, confidence polytope Q_n, coordinatewise lower envelope r_underscore_n, deployed lower-envelope Gibbs policy pi-hat, and diagnostic criterion J_n. Substantial but explicit finite-dimensional construction over Mathlib. ROOT RE-ENCODING SYNC: the fixed sequential coordinate order is defined explicitly by (x',a') earlier than (x,a) iff x'<x or (x'=x and a'<a); PredictionLexLT requires equality at every such earlier coordinate and strict prediction inequality at the first differing coordinate, and this same predicate is used unchanged by both ERM and stabilized selectors. SELECTION-GATE FIX (round 2): the measurability obligation for the SELECTED learner (that f-hat, the coordinatewise lower-envelope minima r_underscore_n(x,a)=min_{f in Q_n} f(x,a), and the resulting Gibbs normalization are measurable in (D_n,E), i.e. pi-hat in L_n(E)) is discharged HERE by an explicit FINITE-DIMENSIONAL measurable-selector lemma (planned as a co-located helper `predictionPolytopeLearner_measurable` in this file), NOT by the cited lem:measurable-maximum-theorem. DISCRETE-SUPPORT SYNC (this round): this helper is scoped to the paper's discrete finite supports via the standing MeasurableSingletonClass instances on X and A now carried by the S1 world (design decision f2.5-discrete-support, added assumption finite-support-discrete-measurability); they are ambient instance arguments of the declaration, and they are what let the finite-dimensional selector argument go through without invoking any cited measurable-selection interface. DECISION-CLASS SYNC (this round — SUPERSEDES the prior claim that L_n(E) does not require reference-supportedness): L_n(E) IS the reference-supported class, so membership of pi-hat now has TWO obligations, both discharged here: (a) measurability in (D_n,E), as above; and (b) SUPPORTEDNESS — the core records that the deployed Gibbs policy satisfies supp pi-hat(.|x) = supp pi_ref(.|x) at every context, which is immediate from the Gibbs formula (the numerator pi_ref(a|x)e^{eta r} vanishes exactly when pi_ref(a|x) does, and the normalizer is a finite strictly positive sum), 'and therefore belongs to the finite-objective decision class'. Plan a co-located `predictionPolytopeLearner_supported` alongside `predictionPolytopeLearner_measurable`; the pair is what downstream theorems cite for `pi-hat in L_n(E)`. Note also that J_underscore_n is retained as a DIAGNOSTIC criterion on reference-supported policies only and does NOT define pi-hat. This is tractable build-inline because every selection is over a compact polytope Q_n subset of finite-dim prediction space R^S with a continuous (linear for the lower envelope, quadratic for the ERM step) objective and the FIXED lexicographic tie-break over the ordered finite set S: measurability follows from continuity/compactness + the explicit deterministic lexicographic construction over Mathlib (Continuous, IsCompact, MeasurableSet, argmin of a continuous function on a compact set). This self-contained learner-measurability lemma is what every downstream consumer (thm:localized-upper and thm:erm-plugin-upper via def:erm-gibbs-plugin-learner, as well as thm:clean-temperature-feature-upper) cites for its `learner in L_n(E)` claim, closing the previously-silent selection gate for ALL three theorems. (thm:clean-temperature-feature-upper additionally invokes the cited lem:measurable-maximum-theorem for its idealized global-optimization stabilized selector, whose inner sup-over-correspondence objective is not covered by this finite-dim lemma; the basic f-hat/lower-envelope measurability above is self-contained.) Build-inline. SEARCH TRACE for the MEASURABLE LEXICOGRAPHIC SELECTOR (re-runnable; the substantive absent object of this node): (1) Causalean, concept words `selector`, `measurable_selection`, `MeasurableSelect`, `argmin`, `lex` — `grep -rniE 'measurable_selection|MeasurableSelect|exists_measurable_selection|selector' ../Causalean` returns 7 files, of which the only statistical hit is Causalean/Stat/MEstimation/FinitePoisson.lean:316 `uniqueGlobalMax_maximizerOrZero` (a `maximizerOrZero` TOTAL selector on a bare type under a UNIQUE-global-max hypothesis: no measurability conclusion, no tie-break, and our ERM/lower-envelope argmins are NOT unique, so it does not fit); the remaining hits (Mathlib/Optimization/SimplexTruncation*, PO/ID/Partial/BalkePearl/LatentTable, SCM/ID/Density/{IdentifyMass,FiniteReference}) are simplex-truncation and identification-density constructions with no selector-measurability statement. `grep -rnE '^(theorem|lemma|def|noncomputable def) \S*([Aa]rgmin|[Ll]ex)' ../Causalean` returns only Panel/Weighted/WLS.lean `proj_eq_argmin` / `residualize_orth_iff_argmin` (a projection CHARACTERIZATION, not a selector). (2) The nearest ERM module, Causalean/Stat/Concentration/UniformDeviation/ERMOracle.lean, was read: `erm_excess_le_two_uniformDeviation` (line 41) TAKES `(ihat istar : ι)` with an ERM inequality `hERM` as a HYPOTHESIS — it never constructs the minimizer and never asserts its measurability, so it cannot discharge this obligation; same for `erm_oracle_inequality` / `erm_oracle_inequality_separable`. (3) Mathlib, `grep -rnE 'Measurable.*argmin|measurable.*[Ss]elect|Measurable.*lex' .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib` -> 3 files, all unrelated (Probability/Moments/ComplexMGF, MeasureTheory/MeasurableSpace/Instances, MeasureTheory/Function/SpecialFunctions/Basic); `lean_local_search 'measurableSelection'` -> [] and `lean_local_search 'measurable_of_isCompact'` -> []. RESULT: NOT FOUND — no Causalean or Mathlib declaration produces a measurable minimizer selector for a continuous objective over a compact set. What Mathlib DOES supply, and what this node's helper is built from: `IsCompact.exists_isMinOn` / `ContinuousOn.exists_isMinOn'` (Mathlib/Topology/Order/Compact.lean, verified present) for existence of the coordinatewise minima on the compact polytope Q_n, plus the FIXED lexicographic tie-break over the ordered finite set S, which turns existence into a deterministic finite-stage construction whose measurability is proved by the explicit recursion (each stage cuts by an equality on a previously-fixed coordinate, a measurable condition) rather than by any selection theorem. This is why the node is build-inline (small, explicit, finite-dimensional) rather than routed to the cited lem:measurable-maximum-theorem, which is reserved for the sup-over-correspondence objective at thm:clean-temperature-feature-upper.

def:minimax-risk.notes: MINIMAX-RISK RE-ENCODING (this round — SUPERSEDES the prior 'no PolicySupportedOn conjunct' note, which now contradicts the core). R_{n,E}(M) = inf over pi-tilde in L_n(E) (the REFERENCE-SUPPORTED class) of sup over P in M of E_{P^otimes n}[J_{eta,P}(pi_P^star) - J_{eta,P}(pi-tilde(D_n;E))]. Three obligations this node now owns, all build-inline: (1) the public contextwise support repair S_ref, defined by the core's two-case formula (keep pi(.|x) when pi is already reference-supported at x, else fall back to pi_ref(.|x)); (2) S_ref is BOREL MEASURABLE and maps every measurable full-simplex learner into L_n(E) — this is exactly where added assumption finite-support-discrete-measurability (design decision f2.5-discrete-support) is load-bearing, since on finite supports with MeasurableSingletonClass the case split is a finite measurable partition, so no separate measurable-selection machinery is needed and the CITED lem:measurable-maximum-theorem is NOT required here; (3) repair never increases regret (off-support at a positive-rho-mass context gives objective -infinity hence regret +infinity, while the repaired regret is finite; when every offending context is rho-null the objective is unchanged), so the supported infimum EQUALS the full-simplex infimum taken in [0,+infinity]. Since pi_P^star has exactly the support of pi_ref and the public reference learner has finite regret, the common minimax value is a NONNEGATIVE REAL — encode the codomain as a real, not an extended real. The scalar minimaxMiss substrate remains an abstraction mismatch (define-local over Mathlib).

def:sample-complexity.notes: SCAFFOLD REDIRECT SYNC (round 11): the tagged sampleComplexity declaration now has proof-bearing arguments for both 0<eps and eps<1, faithfully realizing the declared core space epsilon in (0,1). The untagged companion sampleComplexityPositive uses the identical infimum formula on the all-positive extension needed by the paper's boundary-shell, zero-risk E0, and experiment-uniform lower-bound-ceiling clauses, which explicitly quantify over every eps>0. The separate clean inversion theorems use sampleComplexity and retain their stated 0<eps<1 hypotheses. N*_E(eps;d,C,D,eta)=inf{n in N : R_{n,E}(M_E(d,C,D,eta))<=eps}, with the convention inf(emptyset)=infinity, so the codomain is N u {infinity}. Defined only for M_E(d,C,D,eta) nonempty. It inherits R_{n,E} from def:minimax-risk, hence the REFERENCE-SUPPORTED finite-objective decision class; by the support-repair equality proved there this is the same value as the full-simplex formulation. The sample-size index begins at one, which makes the zero-risk conclusions N*=1 rather than N*=0.

lem:bounded-projection-concentration.notes: GENERAL-CONDITIONAL FIX (round 5 — SUPERSEDES the round-4 ATOM-BRIDGE plan, which realized only the finite-cell partition instance and left the non-atomic case as an F3 contingency; that is now explicitly NOT the plan). The core statement is CONDITIONAL ON AN ARBITRARY SIGMA-FIELD G, and the plan proves it in that generality. Headline Lean declaration `bounded_projection_concentration` takes (m : MeasurableSpace Omega) (hm : m <= mOmega) as an ARBITRARY conditioning sub-sigma-field (no atomicity, no finite-partition hypothesis), an m-measurable projector-valued map Pi with rank at most d, conditional centering E[eps_i | m] = 0, |eps_i| <= 1, conditional independence of (eps_i) given m, and concludes the a.e. conditional tail bound mu[indicator {||Pi eps||_2^2 > 8(d log5 + log(2/zeta))} | m] <= zeta. GENERAL ROUTE (conditional sub-Gaussian + net, done entirely with Mathlib's regular-conditional-distribution layer — this is the delivery, not a fallback): work under the conditional expectation kernel kappa = `ProbabilityTheory.condExpKernel mu m` against `mu.trim hm` (available because the sample space Omega = (S x [0,1])^n is standard Borel and nonempty; recorded in the S1 world notes). Then (G1) CONDITIONAL SUB-GAUSSIAN MGF for a fixed direction: Mathlib defines `ProbabilityTheory.HasCondSubgaussianMGF m hm X c mu` as `Kernel.HasSubgaussianMGF X c (condExpKernel mu m) (mu.trim hm)` (Mathlib/Probability/Moments/SubGaussian.lean:549, verified), i.e. an a.e.-fiber MGF bound; for a.e. fiber the summand v_i eps_i is centered (`condExp_ae_eq_integral_condExpKernel`, Kernel/Condexp.lean:256) and lies in [-|v_i|,|v_i|], so Hoeffding's lemma `ProbabilityTheory.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_mem_Icc_of_integral_eq_zero` (SubGaussian.lean:843, verified) applies FIBERWISE and gives the exp(t^2 v_i^2/2) factor with NO atomicity used. (G2) SUMMATION: Mathlib's conditional independence `ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepFun` (Probability/Independence/Conditional.lean, verified) is BY DEFINITION kernel independence, and `Kernel.iIndepSets` is literally the a.e.-fiber product identity (Probability/Independence/Kernel/Indep.lean:70-71, verified), so for a.e. fiber the eps_i are independent under kappa omega' and `HasSubgaussianMGF.sum_of_iIndepFun` (SubGaussian.lean:768) yields E[exp(t v^T eps) | m] <= exp(t^2/2) a.e. using sum_i v_i^2 = 1; equivalently `Kernel.HasSubgaussianMGF.add_comp` / `.add_compProd` (SubGaussian.lean:491,521) assemble the summands at kernel level. Where the direction v is itself m-measurable (it is: v ranges over a net of the range of the m-measurable Pi), the m-measurable factor is pulled out of the conditional expectation by the standard pull-out-what-is-known lemmas, or equivalently v is kappa omega'-a.e. constant on each fiber (an m-measurable function equals its own conditional expectation, so its fiber variance vanishes) — either way this is a general measure-theoretic step, not a partition argument. (G3) CONDITIONAL CHERNOFF: `Kernel.HasSubgaussianMGF.measure_ge_le` (SubGaussian.lean:334, verified) is already stated as `forall-ae omega' d(nu), (kappa omega').real {eps <= X} <= exp(-eps^2/(2c))` — precisely a CONDITIONAL probability bound — giving Pr{|v^T eps| >= u | m} <= 2 e^{-u^2/2} a.e. (G4) NET + UNION BOUND, conditionally: the unit sphere of the (at most d)-dimensional range of Pi(omega') has a one-half net N(omega') of cardinality <= 5^d by the disjoint-ball volume argument, and ||Pi eps||_2 <= 2 max_{v in N} |v^T eps|; the union bound over a FINITE net is taken inside the a.e. fiber statement (`Finset` union bound on kappa omega'), then transported back to conditional probabilities via `condExpKernel_ae_eq_condExp` (Kernel/Condexp.lean:220). Taking u^2 = 2{d log5 + log(2/zeta)} gives ||Pi eps||_2^2 <= 4u^2, the claimed inequality. Nothing in (G1)-(G4) uses finiteness of the cells, a finite partition, or MeasurableSingletonClass: the conditioning field is arbitrary and the conclusion is the core's general conditional statement. OPTIONAL CONSUMER COROLLARY (demoted from the round-4 headline): `bounded_projection_concentration_fixed`, the deterministic-Pi unconditional specialization, and the finite-cell instance at G = sigma(W_1,...,W_n) may be emitted as convenience corollaries of the general theorem for the localization call site, but they are DOWNSTREAM of it and may NOT be delivered in its place — a deterministic-Pi or finite-atom-only statement does not discharge this node. lem:multinomial-max-count.notes: P{ max_j N_j > 3d } <= d exp(-d(3log3-2)) for d^2 uniform draws into d cells; each per-cell count N_j is Binomial(d^2,1/d), i.e. the bernoulliCount of the indicator f_j=1{draw=j}. REUSE-MISFIT FIX (round 2): the public tail Causalean.Stat.Concentration.bernoulliCount_upper_tail hard-codes the log2 tilt and yields exponent -a(log2-1/2); at threshold a=3d that gives -3d(log2-1/2), NOT the required -d(3log3-2), so it cannot be reused here. The arbitrary-tilt primitive `bernoulliCount_mgf_le` (which the required exponent needs, evaluated at t=log3) is `private` in BinomialCount.lean and hence not importable. Therefore build-inline the per-cell tail at tilt t=log3: reuse the PUBLIC noncomputable def `bernoulliCount` (and `bernoulliCount_measurable`) as the count representation, re-derive the sum-of-iid-Bernoulli MGF bound mgf(N_j)(s) <= exp(d^2 * (1/d) * (e^s-1)) = exp(d(e^s-1)) via Mathlib `ProbabilityTheory.mgf` + `iIndepFun.mgf_sum` (over S.indep) + `Real.add_one_le_exp`, then Markov `measure_ge_le_exp_mul_mgf` at s=log3 to get Pr{N_j>3d} <= exp(-3d*log3 + d(e^{log3}-1)) = exp(-3d log3 + 2d) = exp(-d(3log3-2)); finish with a union bound over the d cells. Build-inline. Trace: grepped Causalean.Stat.Concentration.TailBounds.BinomialCount for an arbitrary-tilt count tail -> only bernoulliCount_upper_tail/bernoulliCount_lower_tail are public (both fix t=+-log2); bernoulliCount_mgf_le and bernoulli_mgf are `private` -> arbitrary-tilt reuse unavailable, inline over Mathlib mgf machinery.

lem:gibbs-regret-identity.notes: J(pi_P^star)-J(pi) = eta^{-1} E_rho KL(pi || pi_P^star). Gibbs normalizer log-linear identity over finite actions; elementary. Reuse Mathlib finite-KL algebra. ExactShell hyp present (no assumption deps). SEARCH TRACE for a REUSABLE GIBBS / KL IDENTITY (re-runnable; this is the trace the prior round omitted): the object sought is the exponential-tilt regret identity `KL(pi || Gibbs tilt of pi_ref by eta r) = KL(pi || pi_ref) - eta E_pi r + log Z`, equivalently the Donsker-Varadhan / Gibbs variational formula, for an ARBITRARY reference-supported pi. (1) Mathlib information theory: `lean_local_search 'klDiv'` -> the full Mathlib/InformationTheory/KullbackLeibler/Basic.lean API (`klDiv_self`, `klDiv_eq_integral_klFun`, `klDiv_eq_zero_iff`, `klDiv_of_ac_of_integrable`, `klDiv_smul_*`, `klDiv_eq_top_iff`, ...) — all structural/monotonicity facts about klDiv, NO tilt or variational identity. `grep -rn 'tilted' .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/InformationTheory` -> NO MATCHES, i.e. Mathlib's exponential tilt (`MeasureTheory.Measure.tilted`, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Tilted.lean, and `ProbabilityTheory.tilted_mul_apply_cgf`/`tilted_mul_apply_mgf` in Probability/Moments/Tilted.lean, both confirmed present via `lean_local_search 'tilt'`) is NEVER connected to klDiv anywhere in Mathlib. `lean_local_search 'variational'` -> []. So Mathlib supplies the tilt and supplies klDiv but not the bridge this identity IS. (2) Causalean information theory: directory listing `../Causalean/Mathlib/InformationTheory/` = {Fano, ProductKLLeCam, Entropy, ConditionalEntropy, GaussianKL, KLBind, KlDensityTiltExpansion/{Basic,CubicRemainder,KLExpansion}}. The most promising, KlDensityTiltExpansion, was READ: `tiltMeasure` (Basic.lean:44) is the LINEAR density tilt `d(tilt)/dmu = 1 + h*s` for a bounded mean-zero score s, and `klDiv_tiltMeasure_toReal_eq` (KLExpansion.lean:65) states `(klDiv (tiltMeasure mu s h) mu).toReal = int (1 + h s) log(1 + h s) dmu`, with `klDiv_tilt_expansion` (KLExpansion.lean:210) and `abs_klRemainder_le` giving its quadratic-plus-cubic-remainder expansion. NON-FIT on three counts: the tilt is LINEAR (`1 + h s`) not EXPONENTIAL (`e^{eta r}/Z`); the KL is taken in the direction `KL(tilt || base)` whereas this note needs `KL(pi || tilt)` with pi ARBITRARY and only the second argument tilted; and the conclusion is an asymptotic expansion in the tilt scale h, not an exact identity. `KLBind.lean` was checked (`rnDeriv_compProd_right_of_forall_ac`, `klDiv_compProd_right_of_forall_ac`, `klDiv_map_measurableEmbedding`, `klDiv_bind_eq_of_base_recording`): these are chain-rule/transport facts for compositions and bind, orthogonal to a tilt identity. `Entropy.lean` (`entropy`, `entropy_nonneg`, `entropy_le_log_card`, `entropy_const_eq_log_card`) and `ConditionalEntropy.lean` are cardinality/nonnegativity bounds, not identities. `GaussianKL.lean` is the Gaussian closed form, wrong family. (3) Causalean minimax KL layer: `grep -rnE '^(theorem|lemma|noncomputable def|def) \S+' ../Causalean/Stat/Minimax/Pinsker.lean` -> `klFun_lower_bound`, `PinskerBound`, `pinskerBound_of_ac_of_ne_top`, `pinskerBound_pi_iid`, `klForm_two_point_lower_bound(_of_pinsker)`; these are KL LOWER BOUNDS used by the S3 testing argument (and are correctly reused there), never an equality. Fano.lean likewise (`fano_average_error`, `fano_exists_error`). `grep -rniE '(donsker|variational|logSumExp|freeEnergy|logPartition|softmax|gibbs)' ../Causalean` -> 18 files, all false positives (Donsker CLASSES in Stat/EmpiricalProcess, `variational` in NPIV/Tikhonov and ConvexProjection, none an information-theoretic Gibbs identity); `lean_local_search 'Gibbs'` -> [] and `lean_local_search 'klForm'` -> [] (note: lean_local_search does NOT index the sibling Causalean package from this project root — the Causalean facts above were established by direct grep/Read under ../Causalean, which is why the empty search results are not evidence of absence and were not treated as such). RESULT: NOT FOUND — neither Mathlib nor Causalean has the exponential-tilt Gibbs regret/variational identity in any direction or generality. Build-inline and small: over the FINITE action set the identity is pure algebra — take logs in the Gibbs formula to get log(pi/pi_P^star) = log(pi/pi_ref) - eta r_theta + log Z_P, integrate against pi(.|x) then rho, and evaluate J at the Gibbs policy to see J(pi_P^star) = eta^{-1} E_rho log Z_P; finiteness of A makes every normalizer a finite strictly positive sum so `Finset.sum` algebra plus `Real.log_div`/`Real.exp_log` suffices, with no measure-theoretic klDiv API required. defer_tier stays false.
